items.text: Supremum of subsheaves
$F_i\subset F$ subsheaves: $\sup F_i=F'=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\bigoplus_iF_i\to F\bigr)$ = the smallest subsheaf of $F$ containing all $F_i$.
u\in F(S')\ \text{lies in }F'(S')\iff\forall s'\in S'\ \exists\ U'\ni s',\ \exists\, i:\ u|_{U'}\in F_i(U')
Recall
Diagonals, sections, kernels are immersions; separated: $\Delta$ a closed immersion.
Non-separated schemes arise naturally

$X\to S$ a family over a curve, general fibre irreducible, special fibre at $s_0$ with two irreducible components: the covering of $S$ by the sets of components is $S$ with $s_0$ doubled ($S_1\cup S_2$ glued along $S-s_0$).
With $n$ components, $s_0$ is multiplied $n$ times.
Example: the Picard scheme

General fibre $\mathbf P^1$, special fibre two $\mathbf P^1$ meeting in a point: $\operatorname{Pic}$ of a fibre $=\mathbf Z$, and $\mathbf Z\times\mathbf Z$ at $s_0$ (degrees $n_1,n_2$ on the components).
P^0\subset\operatorname{Pic}:\quad \text{fibre }0\ \text{over }S-s_0,\qquad \{(n_1,n_2):n_1+n_2=0\}\simeq\mathbf Z\ \text{over }s_0
$P^0$ = $\mathbf Z$ copies of $S$ glued along $S-s_0$: connected, not quasi-compact, locally of finite type over $S$.
Coherent sheaves
$(X,\mathcal O_X)$ ringed space, $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. Coherent: of finite type, and for every $u\colon\mathcal O_U^n\to\mathcal F|_U$ the kernel is of finite type, i.e. locally
\mathcal O_U^m\to\mathcal O_U^n\xrightarrow{\ u\ }\mathcal F\ \text{exact}
(Serre) Coherent modules are stable under finite sums, kernels, cokernels, images, extensions.
Interesting only if $\mathcal O_X$ is a coherent sheaf of rings; then coherent = of finite presentation.
Theorem. $X$ locally noetherian $\Rightarrow$ $\mathcal O_X$ coherent.
X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\ A\ \text{noetherian}:\quad \ker\bigl((A^n)^\sim\to\tilde A\bigr)=\tilde K,\ \ K\subset A^n\ \text{of finite type}
In general quasi-coherent plus finite presentation replaces coherence.
Open immersion versus open map
A surjective immersion $X\to Y$ (defined by a nil ideal) is an open map, but an open immersion only if an isomorphism; non-zero nil ideals exist iff $Y$ is not reduced.
Induced reduced structure
$Y\subset X$ closed subset. The largest closed subscheme with underlying set $Y$:
\mathcal J_Y(U)=\{f\in\mathcal O_X(U):\ f(x)=0\in\kappa(x)\ \ \forall x\in Y\cap U\}
X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\ Y=V(J),\ J=\sqrt J:\qquad \mathcal J_Y=\tilde J\ \text{quasi-coherent}
$V(\mathcal J_Y)$ has underlying set $Y$, is reduced, and is the unique reduced closed subscheme with set $Y$: the induced reduced structure.
\mathcal J\ \text{defines }Y:\quad V(\mathcal J^{n+1})\ \text{infinitesimal neighborhood of order }n,\qquad \varinjlim\ \text{formal neighborhood}
Immersions that are open maps: defined by a nil ideal in an open subset of $Y$.
Locally noetherian implies quasi-separated
$X$ locally noetherian (e.g. locally of finite type over a field): quasi-compact opens are noetherian spaces, so their intersections are quasi-compact.
$X$ coherent iff $X=\bigcup_{\text{finite}}X_i$ affine with all $X_i\cap X_j$ quasi-compact. $f\colon X\to S$ coherent iff $X|_{S_i}$ coherent for $S=\bigcup S_i$ affine.
Direct image of a quasi-coherent sheaf
Theorem. $f$ coherent, $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent on $X$ $\Rightarrow$ $f_*\mathcal F$ (and $R^if_*\mathcal F$) quasi-coherent.
$S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=\bigcup_{i\in\text{finite}}X_i$ affine, $X_{ij}=X_i\cap X_j$ quasi-compact, $f_i,f_{ij}$ the restrictions of $f$, $\mathcal F_i,\mathcal F_{ij}$ those of $\mathcal F$.
0\to f_*\mathcal F\to\prod_if_{i*}\mathcal F_i\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}f_{ij*}\mathcal F_{ij}\qquad\text{exact}
$f_{i*}\mathcal F_i$ quasi-coherent (affine to affine: restriction of scalars); for $f_{ij*}\mathcal F_{ij}$ repeat the argument with $X_{ij}$ inside an affine, where $X_i\cap X_j$ is affine.
Finiteness of the covering is essential: infinite products of quasi-coherent sheaves are not quasi-coherent ($X=\coprod_IS$, $f_*\mathcal F=\prod\mathcal F_i$).
Extension of quasi-coherent sheaves
$U\subset X$ open with $i\colon U\to X$ coherent (retrocompact: $U\cap$ quasi-compact open is quasi-compact), $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent on $U$.
\mathcal G=i_*\mathcal F\ \text{is quasi-coherent on }X,\qquad \mathcal G|_U=i^*i_*\mathcal F\simeq\mathcal F
